title: Crispy Honey Chili Chicken Thighs
shortDescription: Mezze bar with chicken, hummus, and flatbread for ten
subtitle: Mezze bar with chicken, hummus, and flatbread for ten
description: Grilled lemon-herb chicken, hummus, tzatziki, tabbouleh, feta, olives, and warm pita fill a mezze-style bar. Crew builds plates or wraps with Mediterranean flavors and plenty of fresh herbs.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Crispy Honey Chili Chicken Thighs in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Double-check seasoning after scaling — crew palates run salty after long shifts, so taste the first portion before opening the line.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Marinate and grill chicken
steps.instruction: Marinate thighs in lemon, olive oil, oregano, garlic, and salt 2–24 hours. Grill over medium-high heat 6–7 minutes per side until internal temp reaches 175°F and char marks appear.

steps.title: Rest and slice chicken
steps.instruction: Rest grilled chicken 10 minutes, then slice into strips. Hold in a hotel pan at 165°F with a light drizzle of olive oil to prevent drying.

steps.title: Prep cold mezze components
steps.instruction: Portion hummus, tzatziki, tabbouleh, feta, and olives into separate bowls. Garnish hummus with paprika and olive oil drizzle for visual appeal.

steps.title: Warm pita and set the bar
steps.instruction: Wrap pita in foil and warm at 350°F for 8 minutes. Arrange all components along the line with serving spoons and label each dish clearly. Target oven/smoker temperature: 350°F.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Crispy Honey Chili Chicken Thighs onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 10 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Guide plate builds
steps.instruction: Suggest a sample plate: hummus, chicken, tabbouleh, feta, olives, pita. Encourage wraps or bowls and replenish warm pita from the oven as needed.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Crispy Honey Chili Chicken Thighs — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Add a bowl of marinated chickpeas for a vegetarian protein that fits the theme.
Sumac sprinkled over chicken at service adds authentic tang without extra sauce.
Cucumber rounds and cherry tomatoes fill gaps on the board and add fresh crunch.
tonightSpread: Full Mediterranean mezze bar with grilled chicken, dips, and warm pita.
Simple orzo salad with lemon for crews wanting extra carbs beyond pita.
leftovers: Wrap chicken and dips into lunch pitas with extra tabbouleh.
Stir leftover components into a lemony grain salad for tomorrow.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Mediterranean night breaks the heavy comfort-food cycle without feeling like diet food. Most components are make-ahead, and the spread looks impressive with minimal last-minute cooking.
mealPrepNotes: Marinate chicken overnight. Make hummus and tzatziki up to 2 days ahead. Tabbouleh improves after a few hours in the fridge—make it in the morning.
